title: Skeletal pushouts of a simplicial tensor coend
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category enriched over small simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with chosen tensors and cotensors as in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], and with all small colimits in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $A\otimes K$ for the tensor $K\otimes A$. Let $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ be any simplicial object. For each $n\geq0$ define
$$R_n(X)=\operatorname{coeq}\left(\coprod_{\alpha:[a]\to[b],\;0\leq a,b\leq n}X_b\otimes\Delta^a\rightrightarrows\coprod_{a=0}^nX_a\otimes\Delta^a\right),$$
where $\Delta^a=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}(-,[a])$, and the arrows on the $\alpha$ summand are induced by $X(\alpha)$ and $\Delta^\alpha$. Let $R_{-1}(X)$ be initial. Define $|X|$ by the same coequalizer without the upper bounds. Let $L_nX$ be the colimit over proper order-preserving surjections $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ with $a<n$, assigning $X_a$ to $\theta$; a morphism from $\theta$ to $\theta'$ is a surjection $\rho:[a']\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ with $\theta=\rho\theta'$, and its diagram map is $X(\rho):X_a\to X_{a'}$. The maps $X(\theta)$ induce $\lambda_n:L_nX\to X_n$. Let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of the proper faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Set
$$B_n=(L_nX\otimes\Delta^n)\amalg_{L_nX\otimes\partial\Delta^n}(X_n\otimes\partial\Delta^n).$$
There is a pushout square with top edge $B_n\to R_{n-1}(X)$, left edge the canonical map $B_n\to X_n\otimes\Delta^n$, bottom edge the degree-$n$ coend map $X_n\otimes\Delta^n\to R_n(X)$, and right edge $R_{n-1}(X)\to R_n(X)$.
Here the upper arrow on the latching summand is induced, for each $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, by $X_a\otimes\Delta^n\xrightarrow{1\otimes\Delta^\theta}X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to R_{n-1}(X)$; on a boundary face $\delta:[a]\hookrightarrow[n]$ it is induced by $X_n\otimes\Delta^a\xrightarrow{X(\delta)\otimes1}X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to R_{n-1}(X)$. These maps agree on their overlaps. The truncation inclusions induce a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{colim}_{n\geq0}R_n(X)\cong|X|$. The square and isomorphism are natural in $X$. No model structure or cofibrancy assumption is required.

proof.text: Use composition order $vu=v\circ u$. The tensor representing isomorphism on vertices is $\mathcal C(A\otimes K,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,T))$. For $u:K\to K'$, precomposition on the right defines $1\otimes u:A\otimes K\to A\otimes K'$. Identity, composition and commutation with $f\otimes1$ follow by applying this bijection: both sides are the same precomposition map. Thus the two variables give a bifunctor. This uses precisely the representing isomorphism and its naturality, without any model-category axiom.

proof.text: The tensor preserves the small colimits needed in each variable, directly by their universal properties. For a small diagram $(A_i)$, the tensor/cotensor adjunction identifies maps $(\operatorname{colim}_i A_i)\otimes K\to T$ with maps $\operatorname{colim}_i A_i\to T^K$, hence with compatible families $A_i\to T^K$, hence with compatible families $A_i\otimes K\to T$. For a small diagram $(K_i)$ in simplicial sets, maps $A\otimes\operatorname{colim}_i K_i\to T$ are compatible families $K_i\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,T)$, hence compatible families $A\otimes K_i\to T$. These bijections preserve all cocone maps, which proves the required colimit properties. They also show that tensoring an initial object in either variable is initial.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text: Here is the boundary gluing calculation used below, written from its definition as a union. An $m$-simplex of $\partial\Delta^n$ is a non-surjective monotone map $\phi:[m]\to[n]$. Its image, listed increasingly, gives a proper injection $\delta:[a]\hookrightarrow[n]$ and a surjection $p:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ with $\phi=\delta p$. A family of simplicial maps $h_\delta:\Delta^a\to Z$ compatible under inclusions of proper faces determines the value $h_\delta(p)$ on $\phi$. If another face contains the image of $\phi$, the image face includes into it, so compatibility gives the same value. For $\beta:[l]\to[m]$, the image of $\phi\beta$ is a subface of the image of $\phi$; the same compatibility gives $h(\phi\beta)=Z(\beta)h(\phi)$. Thus the formula defines a unique simplicial map from the boundary. Taking $Z=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A,T)$ and using the tensor bijection, maps $A\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to T$ are exactly compatible maps $A\otimes\Delta^a\to T$ for the proper injective faces. For $n=0$ the family is empty, as is the boundary.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text:
Write $q_a^N:X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to R_N(X)$ for the coequalizer summand maps, and abbreviate $q_a=q_a^{n-1}$ when $a<n$. The coequalizer universal property says that maps $R_N(X)\to T$ are precisely families $t_a:X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to T$, $a\leq N$, satisfying
$$t_a(X(\alpha)\otimes1)=t_b(1\otimes\Delta^\alpha)\quad(\alpha:[a]\to[b],\ a,b\leq N).$$
This is the equality on each summand of the two parallel arrows, so no extra coend theorem is invoked. The maps $q_a^{N+1}$ with $a\leq N$ satisfy these equations and therefore induce the truncation map $R_N\to R_{N+1}$. All index categories are small: finite ordinal objects and their finite hom sets, the countable simplex category, and the natural-number order.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text:
For each proper surjection $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ put $D_\theta=q_a(1\otimes\Delta^\theta):X_a\otimes\Delta^n\to R_{n-1}$. If $\theta=\rho\theta'$ with $\rho:[a']\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, the relation of Step 4 for $\rho$ gives
$$D_\theta=q_a(1\otimes\Delta^\rho)(1\otimes\Delta^{\theta'})=q_{a'}(X(\rho)\otimes1)(1\otimes\Delta^{\theta'})=D_{\theta'}(X(\rho)\otimes1).$$
Both $a,a'<n$, as required for that relation. These are exactly the arrows of the stated latching diagram, with its specified contravariant direction. The colimit property of $L_nX$ and Step 2 give the unique map $D:L_nX\otimes\Delta^n\to R_{n-1}$ with these components.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text:
For every proper injection $\delta:[a]\hookrightarrow[n]$ put $E_\delta=q_a(X(\delta)\otimes1):X_n\otimes\Delta^a\to R_{n-1}$. If $\delta=\delta'\gamma$ with $\gamma:[a]\hookrightarrow[b]$ and $a,b<n$, contravariant functoriality and the lower-degree relation for $\gamma$ give
$$E_\delta=q_a(X(\gamma)\otimes1)(X(\delta')\otimes1)=q_b(1\otimes\Delta^\gamma)(X(\delta')\otimes1)=E_{\delta'}(1\otimes\Delta^\gamma).$$
Step 3 therefore glues these maps uniquely to $E:X_n\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to R_{n-1}$. This also checks all face intersections, since their nonempty image faces are objects of this same proper-face family.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text:
The maps $D$ and $E$ agree on $L_nX\otimes\partial\Delta^n$. By the latching colimit property and Step 3 it suffices to check a surjection $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ and a proper face $\delta:[b]\hookrightarrow[n]$. On $X_a\otimes\Delta^b$ their composites are respectively
$$q_a(1\otimes\Delta^{\theta\delta})\quad\text{and}\quad q_b(X(\delta)X(\theta)\otimes1)=q_b(X(\theta\delta)\otimes1).$$
They agree by Step 4 for $\theta\delta:[b]\to[a]$, whose two degrees are strictly below $n$. This includes the case where $\theta\delta$ is neither injective nor surjective. Hence the pushout defining $B_n$ supplies precisely the upper arrow described in the statement.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text: The canonical map $B_n\to X_n\otimes\Delta^n$ uses $\lambda_n\otimes1$ on the latching summand and the boundary inclusion on the face summand; they agree on their common source by bifunctoriality. The proposed square commutes. On $X_a\otimes\Delta^n$ in the latching summand its equality is the degree-$n$ coequalizer relation for $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$; on $X_n\otimes\Delta^a$ in the boundary summand it is the relation for $\delta:[a]\hookrightarrow[n]$. Steps 2 and 3 and the defining pushout show that these tests determine the maps on $B_n$. Thus the displayed four edges form a commutative square.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text:
Fix any target object $T$, a map $f:R_{n-1}\to T$, and $g:X_n\otimes\Delta^n\to T$. Put $t_a=fq_a$ for $a<n$ and $t_n=g$. By the pushout definition of $B_n$, its latching colimit, and Step 3, the equality of $f$ and $g$ after restriction to $B_n$ is equivalent to exactly the equations
$$t_n(X(\theta)\otimes1)=t_a(1\otimes\Delta^\theta),\qquad t_n(1\otimes\Delta^\delta)=t_a(X(\delta)\otimes1)$$
for every proper surjection $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ and proper injection $\delta:[a]\hookrightarrow[n]$. Necessity follows by restriction; sufficiency follows from uniqueness of the maps on each colimit and then on its pushout. These equations add just the surjection and injection relations involving degree $n$ to the relations already satisfied below degree $n$.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text:
These equations imply every remaining relation of $R_n$, including all nonidentity endomorphisms of $[n]$. Indeed any monotone $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$ factors as $\alpha=\delta\theta$ by listing its image increasingly, with $\theta:[a]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ and $\delta:[k]\hookrightarrow[b]$. Here $k\leq\min(a,b)\leq n$. The relation for $\theta$ is already known if $a<n$, and otherwise is a surjection equation of Step 9 or the identity equation. Similarly the relation for $\delta$ is known if $b<n$, and otherwise is an injection equation or the identity. Their composite is
$$t_a(X(\alpha)\otimes1)=t_a(X(\theta)\otimes1)(X(\delta)\otimes1)=t_k(1\otimes\Delta^\theta)(X(\delta)\otimes1)=t_b(1\otimes\Delta^\delta)(1\otimes\Delta^\theta)=t_b(1\otimes\Delta^\alpha).$$
The middle interchange is tensor bifunctoriality. Conversely every relation of Step 9 is among the relations of $R_n$.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text: By Step 4, the extended family $(t_a)_{a\leq n}$ now induces a unique $h:R_n\to T$. It restricts to $g$ on the degree-$n$ summand and to $f$ on $R_{n-1}$, the latter equality being checked on each $q_a$, $a<n$. Any such $h$ has these same components, hence is equal to this one by the coequalizer property. Together with Step 8, this is exactly the pushout universal property of the square in the statement. The argument establishes existence and uniqueness for every target $T$, rather than assuming a pre-existing skeletal-filtration comparison.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text: For $n=0$, the latching category and proper-face family are empty. Hence $L_0X$ and $X_0\otimes\partial\Delta^0$ are initial by Step 2, $B_0$ is initial, and $R_{-1}$ is initial by definition. The only endomorphism of $[0]$ is its identity, so both arrows of the defining $R_0$ coequalizer coincide and $R_0\cong X_0\otimes\Delta^0$. Thus the same square is a pushout in degree zero as well. No argument presumes a nonempty latching category.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text: Let $R_\infty=\operatorname{colim}_{N\geq0}R_N$. The full coend summand maps give compatible maps $R_N\to|X|$, hence $c:R_\infty\to|X|$. Conversely the component $X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to R_a\to R_\infty$ satisfies the full coend relation for every $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$: choose $N=\max(a,b)$ and use that relation in $R_N$, then compose to $R_\infty$. Hence the full coequalizer gives $d:|X|\to R_\infty$. On every full coend summand $cd$ is the identity. On every summand of each $R_N$, $dc$ followed by $R_N\to R_\infty$ equals that same map. The coequalizer uniqueness and then the sequential-colimit uniqueness therefore give $cd=1$ and $dc=1$. This proves the claimed isomorphism with its specified comparison map.

source.place: Formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed p.10; tensor adjunctions in Section 19.1, printed p.90. The categorical universal-property calculation below is agent-written; the source leaves the pushout verification unstated.

proof.text: For a natural transformation $u:X\to Y$, the maps $u_a\otimes1$ respect the coequalizer relations because $u_aX(\alpha)=Y(\alpha)u_b$. They induce all truncation and full-coend maps. On every latching component, $u_nX(\theta)=Y(\theta)u_a$ gives the induced latching map; on every boundary face, $u_aX(\delta)=Y(\delta)u_n$ gives compatibility of the face attaching map. The colimit and pushout uniqueness give the commuting maps of the displayed squares. The comparison $c$ of Step 13 commutes with $u$ on every summand, and so does its inverse by uniqueness. This proves both asserted naturality clauses. Only the stated tensor/cotensor and colimit hypotheses have been used.

lean.statement: theorem tensor_coend_skeletal_pushouts (T : SimplicialTensorCotensor C) : (∀ X : SimplicialObject C, Nonempty (IsInitial (stage T X 0))) ∧ (∀ (X : SimplicialObject C) (n : ℕ), IsUpperMap T X n (upperMap T X n) ∧ IsPushout (upperMap T X n) (attachingTo T X n) (stageMap T (𝟙 X) (Nat.le_succ n)) (stageι T X (n + 1) ⦋n⦌ (Nat.lt_succ_self n))) ∧ (∀ X : SimplicialObject C, ∃ e : colimit (sequence T X) ≅ SimplicialModelRealization.realization T X, (∀ n : ℕ, colimit.ι (sequence T X) n ≫ e.hom = toRealization T X (n + 1)) ∧ (∀ (Y : SimplicialObject C) (f : X ⟶ Y) (eY : colimit (sequence T Y) ≅ SimplicialModelRealization.realization T Y), (∀ n : ℕ, colimit.ι (sequence T Y) n ≫ eY.hom = toRealization T Y (n + 1)) → ∃! c : colimit (sequence T X) ⟶ colimit (sequence T Y), (∀ n : ℕ, colimit.ι (sequence T X) n ≫ c = stageMap T f (le_refl (n + 1)) ≫ colimit.ι (sequence T Y) n) ∧ c ≫ eY.hom = e.hom ≫ SimplicialModelRealization.map T f)) ∧ (∀ {X Y : SimplicialObject C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ), ∃! b : attaching T X n ⟶ attaching T Y n, IsAttachingMap T f n b ∧ b ≫ upperMap T Y n = upperMap T X n ≫ stageMap T f (le_refl n) ∧ b ≫ attachingTo T Y n = attachingTo T X n ≫ T.tensorMap (SSet.stdSimplex.obj ⦋n⦌) (f.app (op ⦋n⦌)))
